assumptions: Loop vectors are valid vectors: begin <= end, end - begin is a multiple of the element step, and the element count matches the span; the model raises otherwise.

A string's ptr field for an empty or inline string points at its own +0x10 slot, which is the binary's inline-form test; a zero ptr with a heap flag is not a realistic string and is not given a special case.
Plain vectors' end fields are not read by this routine, so they are not modelled; only begin (zero test) and cap (size) matter.

callees.call_count_in_routine: many, one per destroyed heap string, plain vector, array and list node
callees.contract: operator delete with (pointer, size); the two tail strings return through it
called once per list node with the node's +0x18 qword; return discarded; its own semantics are not claimed

census.note: All 87 direct call sites are listed by address in callers.tsv and reproduced by census.py; they are not individually excerpted, because the routine's whole-function window plus its visit-routine consumer carry the behavior. The visit-routine call at 0x5f6eafa is excerpted in consumer.txt.

consumer.note: The element-visit-and-reset routine (open PR #2383) calls this routine once per element pointer, stepping 0x180 per element; its return is discarded. That routine's element size 0x180 matches this routine's highest field, the string at +0x160..+0x180.

distinct_from: Open PR #2383 (element-visit-and-reset routine 0x5f6eac0): that routine is this routine's consumer, not this routine; no address overlap in the routine windows.
Open PR #2376 (teardown pair 0x5f78000/0x5f78030): different functions, different fields, no address overlap.
No open PR title or code search hit for 0x5d516f0.

fields.rule: if ptr != address of the +0x170 slot, delete(ptr, qword at +0x170 + 1); otherwise no delete
if ptr != address of the +0x148 slot, delete(ptr, qword at +0x148 + 1); otherwise no delete
if begin at +0x110 is nonzero, delete(begin, qword at +0x120 - begin); end at +0x118 is never read
if begin at +0xf8 is nonzero, delete(begin, qword at +0x108 - begin); end at +0x100 is never read
walk begin at +0xe0 to end at +0xe8 in 0x58 steps, destroying each element's two strings by the string rule, then if begin is nonzero delete(begin, qword at +0xf0 - begin)
walk begin at +0xc8 to end at +0xd0 in 0x130 steps, destroying each element's four strings by the string rule, then if begin is nonzero delete(begin, qword at +0xd8 - begin)
for each node from head at +0xa8: call 0x5d4c8d0 with the node's +0x18 qword, delete(node, 0x30), then follow next at +0x10, until zero
walk begin at +0x80 to end at +0x88 in 0x28 steps, destroying each element's string by the string rule, then if begin is nonzero delete(begin, qword at +0x90 - begin)
if ptr != address of the +0x38 slot, tail-jump to delete(ptr, qword at +0x38 + 1); otherwise return
if ptr != address of the +0x18 slot, tail-jump to delete(ptr, qword at +0x18 + 1); otherwise return

not_claimed: The 0x5d4c8d0 callee's semantics or effects beyond its call contract.
Caller semantics beyond the visit-routine consumer site; the other 86 call sites are census addresses only, not individually modelled.
Any meaning for the fields beyond the offsets and rules stated here, or for what the visited elements denote.
Any field the routine never reads, including obj+0x00 and the plain vectors' end fields.
